hints: Insert lights in the order given; each one splits one existing gap into two.
Track the current gap lengths and the largest gap.
A multiset keeps duplicate gap lengths, while an ordered set of positions finds the neighbors.
analogy: A new traffic light cuts one road segment into two smaller segments.
example: On road length 10, inserting at 4 splits length 10 into 4 and 6; the largest gap is 6.
algorithm: Keep positions including 0 and x in an ordered set and gap lengths in a multiset. For p, find neighbors l,r, erase r-l, insert p-l and r-p, then print the largest gap.
correctness: Only the gap containing p changes; replacing it with its two parts maintains the exact set of current road gaps.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
